neutral_facts.value: The accused, a married couple, were alleged to have forged the signature of the husband on a passport application for their minor child. The husband, who was living abroad, had allegedly abandoned the wife and child in India. The wife sought to obtain a passport for the child, and the husband later filed a complaint alleging forgery. The investigating agency filed a chargesheet, but the Supreme Court found that the evidence was inconclusive and that the proceedings were an abuse of the process of law. The Court quashed the FIR and all related proceedings, finding that the allegations did not meet the necessary legal standards for the charges brought against the accused.

investigation_status.value: Supplementary charge-sheet filed on 25.07.2017, investigation deemed lacking in rigour and failed to satisfy s.173(8) Cr.P.C.

quotes.text: The investigating agency acted mechanically, in purported compliance with the Trial Magistrate’s order.

procedural_irregularity.value: The supplementary chargesheet relied on the Truth Lab report, which was already available when the original chargesheet was filed, and failed to satisfy the requisites of s.173(8) Cr.P.C.

quotes.text: The term ‘further investigation’ stipulated in s.173(8) Cr.P.C. obligates the officer-in-charge of the concerned police station to ‘obtain further evidence, oral or documentary’, and only then forward a supplementary report regarding such evidence, in the prescribed form.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellants forged the signature of respondent No. 2 on the passport application, thereby constituting the offence of cheating u/s. 420 IPC and forgery u/ss. 468 and 471 IPC. They also alleged a violation of s.12(b) of the Passports Act, 1967, and sought further investigation under s.173(8) Cr.P.C.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the actions of the appellants did not constitute deceit or damage, as the passport was obtained for the minor child's benefit and not at the cost of respondent No. 2. They contended that the State FSL report was inconclusive and that the supplementary chargesheet lacked new evidence, thus violating procedural requirements.
